_doc: Single source of truth for per-model NPU export geometry. Consumed by tools/export/export_gemm_rtp.py (S2+). Geometry MUST match runtime/src/common/hub.cpp (catalog table lines 52-142 and the bfp16 adoption list lines 161-168); tools/verify_targets.py (S7) enforces parity. Mapping rules: datapath 'bfp16' -> --emulate-bfp16 --c-bf16; datapath 'bf16' -> --c-bf16 only; qkv_n null -> --qkv-n omitted (means 3*hidden); model.overrides.* beats defaults.* for that model; arches[N] supplies --cols/--batch/--batches; max_batch is a hard per-arch ceiling. datapath flag mapping lives in code (S2), not here, to avoid duplication. WHISPER (kind 'stt') adds keys the embedders do not have: heads/head_dim/enc_layers/dec_layers/mel_bins, `frames` (the model's TRUE encoder length, 1500, from max_source_positions -- the number of positions that must be computed, not the number of rows a design holds) and `max_target` (448 decoder positions). Whisper's encoder is NOT one dispatch. A shim has 16 DMA buffer descriptors and a design's live count grows with its AIE row-block count, so a single dispatch cannot exceed FOUR row-blocks: measured on npu1 with m=64/rows=4, M=256/512/1024 build and run, M=1536 and M=2048 fail to compile with \'Too many simultaneously active buffer descriptors\' and M=1536 with the derived C-path ping-pong additionally times out with ERT_CMD_STATE_TIMEOUT. 1500 rows therefore becomes 3 dispatches of 512, and `overrides.seq` is 512 -- the per-dispatch row tile, NOT frames. The runtime loops ceil(padded_frames / design.seq) times; the last chunk is padded and its extra rows are masked, which is exact because every encoder GEMM is row-independent (attention lives on the host over all 1500 positions). The padded total is 1536, i.e. 2.4% waste; a 1024-wide design would cut dispatch count to 2 at the price of 36.5% wasted arithmetic, which is the worse trade by two orders of magnitude at these sizes. The DECODER is a second design set (kinds.stt, written to gemm_rtp_dec/): its M is tokens per step, not frames, and it uses m=16 rather than 64 so its smallest M is 64 rather than 256 -- see tools/export/exporters/gemm_rtp/geometry.py for why it still uses four AIE rows. Per-model `batches` exists because an STT model's unit of work is one audio file, not a batch of texts, so its tiers may be 1. tile_k 64 / tile_n 32 is forced by Whisper's geometry, not chosen: d % 64 == 0 and (d/32) % 4 == 0 for every d in {384,512,768,1024,1280}, so no operand needs padding; tile_n 48 does not divide large-v3's 5120 FFN. IMAGE CLASSIFIER (kind 'cls', arch 5 vit_patch16_prenorm_gelu) -- vit-base-patch16-224 is the fourth family and the second MODALITY. Its geometry is an embedder's geometry: the same four streams at the same shapes (768x2304, 768x768, 768x3072, 3072x768), because its patch-embedding conv is rewritten as an exact GEMM that RIDES attn_out's stream [M,768]x[768,768] rather than asking the array for a convolution it has no role for. That rewrite is exact on one ground and one only: stride equals kernel with padding 0, so the 196 windows neither overlap nor skip and im2col is a PERMUTATION, not a sum. What is new is the front end (decode, resize, normalise, im2col) and the head (a 768x1000 matvec on the host, because 1000 is not a multiple of tile_n*cols so no B panel of that width exists on this array, and one host matvec costs less than the ~150 us a dispatch would). Its overrides.seq of 256 is a ROW TILE, not a sequence length: a ViT's position count is FIXED at (image_size/patch_size)^2 + 1 = 197 (196 patches plus the CLS row), which is why no --max-seq-style knob exists for this family, and the runtime pads 197 up to 256 and masks the remainder -- exact, because every GEMM here is row-independent and attention lives on the host over all 197 positions. batch 4 gives M = 1024 in one dispatch, the npu1 ceiling measured above. Attention at 197 positions has been MEASURED on this container since that note was written: the encoder runs 0.349 s with `--npu-ops attn` against 0.244 s on the host (the array SLOWER), and `attn,softm` together is 6.685 s because NpuAttention calls the softmax per head per chunk while every call fills the design's whole row capacity. So this entry's throughput is a measurement rather than a hole, and `attn` is offered here for correctness on the array, not for speed.

cls.note: arch 5, vit_patch16_prenorm_gelu. The stream list is gemm_rtp's VERBATIM and that is the claim being made: this family's five GEMMs ride the four streams an embedder already has, at the embedder's shapes -- patch_embed is [M,768]x[768,768], which IS attn_out's shape, and qkv / attn_out / ffn_up / ffn_down are [768,2304] / [768,768] / [768,3072] / [3072,768]. A new modality here is a new FRONT END (decode, resize, im2col) and a new HEAD (1000 logits on the host), not a new array. `seq` here is the per-dispatch ROW TILE the 197 positions are padded into, not a text sequence length: 196 patches + 1 CLS = 197, padded to 256. batch 4 puts M = 1024 in one dispatch, which is the npu1 ceiling -- a shim has 16 DMA buffer descriptors and a design's live count grows with its AIE row-block count, so four row-blocks is the measured maximum and M=1536 fails to compile.

pose.note:
arch 6, yolov8_pose_c2f_silu_dfl.

The FIRST stream set in this file whose streams are not operation names. The fourteen `conv{K}x{N}` entries are the network's own padded convolution shapes, in the order gemm_rtp/geometry.py's POSE_CONV_SHAPES gives them, and this list is written out rather than derived because the targets schema requires `streams` to be a list -- which makes the two independent spellings of one list, and tools/verify/verify_pose_streamset.py is what holds them together: it checks this file against geometry.py, against the design set's design.json, and against the packed container's npu_streams, all four ways.

M is ONE value for the whole set, not one per stride, and that is why no stream name carries an M. The runtime reads its row count once from the design's top-level M (runtime/src/pose/session.cpp) and cuts every convolution into chunks of it (runtime/src/pose/net.cpp), so a set with a stream per (K, N, M) would have twenty-one streams of which four are dispatched and the rest unreachable.

hands.note:
arch 7, mediapipe_hands_palm_ssd_lm_heatmap. TWO graphs in one container -- a 87-node palm detector and a 58-node hand-landmark network -- and the twelve `conv{K}x{N}` entries are the union of what their dense convolutions pad to, listed so the set is named rather than implied.

The padding is gemm_rtp/geometry.py's, and the raw count is worth stating next to the padded one: the 61 dense convolutions have 31 distinct RAW (K, N) pairs, of which K up to a multiple of tile_k = 64 and N up to a multiple of tile_n*cols = 128 leaves twelve, the two graphs sharing (64,128) and (128,128). Twelve is fewer than pose's fourteen, whose set exists and was measured, so the shapes are not what stands between this model and the array.

NO DESIGN SET CARRIES THIS LIST. It is written down so the claim can be checked, not so something can be dispatched on it: runtime/include/runtime/hands_mode.hpp REFUSES --npu-ops conv for this architecture by name, because there is no array timing to compare the host's against and running on the host under that flag would report host numbers as array ones. Nothing in this tree builds these twelve yet.

M is ONE value for the whole set, as in pose: the dispatch chunk is the design's single top-level row count and every convolution is cut into chunks of it, because the runtime has nowhere to keep twelve different row counts. The 39 depthwise convolutions in the container are deliberately NOT in this list -- a depthwise filter reduces within one channel and has no [M, N] GEMM to dispatch, so a stream for it would be a name with nothing behind it.

mppose.note:
arch 8, mediapipe_pose_det_ssd_lm_regress. TWO graphs in one container -- a 93-node person detector and a 120-node pose-landmark network -- and the twenty-two `conv{K}x{N}` entries are the union of what their dense convolutions pad to, counted off the packed container rather than written by hand.

The padding is gemm_rtp/geometry.py's, and the raw count is worth stating next to the padded one: the 99 dense convolutions have 53 distinct RAW (K, N) pairs across the two graphs, of which K up to a multiple of tile_k = 64 and N up to a multiple of tile_n*cols = 128 leaves TWENTY-TWO -- fifteen from the detector and thirteen from the landmark network, which share four. That is more than pose's fourteen and more than hands' twelve, and it is the largest set in this file. It is also the only one of the three whose set has never been built by anything, which is what decides whether it is worth having.

NO DESIGN SET CARRIES THIS LIST. It is written down so the claim can be checked, not so something can be dispatched on it: runtime/include/runtime/mppose_mode.hpp REFUSES --npu-ops conv for this architecture by name, because there is no array timing to compare the host's against and running on the host under that flag would report host numbers as array ones. The numbers a design set would have to beat, measured here: onnxruntime's float run of the same two graphs is 5.29 ms + 6.56 ms = 11.69 ms for one person on docs/bus.jpg at 16 threads, and this build's host fp32 walk is 49.7 ms + 70.6 ms = 120.3 ms for the same frame.

M is ONE value for the whole set, as in pose and hands. TWO THINGS IN THIS CONTAINER WILL NOT MOVE WHATEVER THE SET SAYS. 62 of its 161 convolutions are DEPTHWISE -- 28 of the detector's 73 and 34 of the landmark network's 88, carrying 77.2M MAC, 12.3 % of the container -- and a depthwise filter reduces within one channel, so there is no [M, N] GEMM in it to dispatch and a stream for it would be a name with nothing behind it. And the architecture has an op that is not a GEMM at all: three DepthToSpace steps, which are pure plane copies, and which is how the detector builds its 28/14/7 pyramid out of a single 7x7 map.
